We give you your own private codebase and database. Set up for you, step by step.

How this works — the facts

Someone shared this with you so your AIs actually remember you.

No account with us.

  • No payment. Everything sits under your own accounts.
    A private codebase and a database.
  • GitHub. If sign-in fails, a code option sits under “Having trouble?”.
    Never a fake “connected”.
  • Supabase. Same deal.
    A code option if sign-in fails.
  • AI tools. One paste each. No shared sign-in exists across them.
    So each gets a ready-to-paste block.
  • Your passwords stay yours. They never go in your folder. No server of ours touches them.
    Codes you paste are checked in your browser only. Never saved.
  • “Done” means checked. A step counts only when the service itself says it worked.
    If it complains, we show you its exact words.
  • You start from everyone's best setups — one shared register.
  • You never sync anything yourself. Your AIs do it for you.

      Your folder is built. Now for its memory — the part that lets your AIs remember you.

      What happened, in technical words
      Downloads a picture of your home as it looks today — nice for sharing the news.
      Your AIs can't see this by themselves. One paste per AI — this message does the rest.
      Paste once into each app.
      Copy-paste messages
      The one safety rule:
      • Everything created is private and yours: repo under your GitHub, database under your Supabase.
      • This page keeps no copy of your tokens or keys.
      • To cut access: revoke the token in the provider's settings, delete keys from your local .env.
      • Now revoke the two setup tokens you pasted. Setup is done, and they've served their purpose.
      Confirm each app is wired: paste it this message
      How to read the reply:
      • Correct verification phrase + correct facts = strong evidence it's wired. Not proof.
      • Wrong or missing phrase = not wired. Even if the rest sounds plausible.
      • It names a blank field = wired, just not filled in yet. Not a failure.
      • It says “I can't read your agent home yet” = not wired. Paste the full setup block from CONNECT.md first.
      Send the matching message to each AI app you use. It asks the app to reply with: the verification phrase from MEMORY.md (verbatim), your name from USER.md, one fact from MEMORY.md (word for word), and the canonical-store line.
      Full setup blocks
      The longer first-time blocks (also saved as CONNECT.md in your repo). There is no shared one-click sign-in across these tools. A generated paste block is the honest version.
      Your local .env. Save this, never commit it
      This is the only key file an AI app may ever draw from, and the only key in it is SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.
      .env.service-role (importer only — never give this to any AI app)
      Save this as a separate local file next to your .env. Only the importer (tools/import_md.py) on your own machine uses it. It has full access to your database.
      Read back from your home just now.

      Optional: GitHub Secrets (manual — this page does not do this for you)
      • Only needed if you later run GitHub Actions against your database. Most people never need it.
      • This page doesn't do it for you. Adding secrets needs GitHub's encryption flow.
      • Manual path: your repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret.
      • Add SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY from your local .env, one at a time.
      • Add SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY only if an Action truly needs it. It has full access.
